sections.h2: Who is Pembroke Pines, and who buys homes here?
sections.html:
The city places itself in southwest Broward and reports more than 170,000 residents. It describes easy reach of major highways, jobs, parks and golf courses.

It was incorporated on January 16, 1960, when it was the Village of Pembroke Pines with about 1,500 residents. After Hurricane Andrew in 1992 the city's own history says it became the fastest growing city in the country, which is why so much housing dates from the 1990s and later.

Buyers here range from families drawn to its schools and parks to residents of the Century Village area. The city counts 41 arts and cultural facilities and describes its mission around raising a family.

sections.h2: How did Pembroke Pines grow, and what does that say about house age?
sections.html:
The area was open land and small communities, including the Pembroke Pines Country Club development, in the mid 20th century. Fire stations opened as the city expanded: Station 79 in 1981 in land annexed west of US 27 and Station 89 in 1986 at Century Village.

  • Land west of US 27 was annexed by 1981, so house age varies by side of town.
  • Check roof, electrical and plumbing age on your own house.
  • Ask a title agent what recorded items exist on your lot.

Knowing your home's age helps you decide whether a cash offer or listing fits. Six fire stations now serve the city, and in 2014 it joined the Broward County Regional 911 system.

sections.h2: What does Florida charge to transfer a Pembroke Pines house?
sections.html:
Broward is not Miami-Dade, so the deed rate is 70 cents per $100 of consideration. Each party to the document is liable.

Taxable documents the state lists for real estate transfers
DocumentTaxed by DOR?
Warranty deedYes
Quit claim deedYes
Deed in lieu of foreclosure saleYes
Personal representative deed under probated willNot taxable

The clerk of court collects the tax when recording. Ask your closing agent to apply the rate to your price in writing.

sections.h2: How does the Broward County tax cycle affect a seller?
sections.html:
The Broward appraiser values property on January 1 and takes exemption filings through March 1. Its site gives 954-357-6830 for questions.

  • August brings the proposed tax notice.
  • November bills carry the largest early payment discount, 4 percent.
  • April 1 marks delinquency.

Your closing agent splits the year's tax between you and the buyer, so confirm the split reflects your exemption status.

sections.h2: Does homestead or portability matter if I leave Pembroke Pines?
sections.html:
It can, particularly after many years of ownership. Save Our Homes has kept your assessment growth at 3 percent or CPI, whichever is lower, and portability may move up to $500,000 of the savings to a new Florida home.

The new homestead has to begin within three years of the January 1 that follows the old one being given up. Form DR-501T goes in with the DR-501 by March 1. The statute page notes later amendments first apply to the 2027 roll, so confirm current rules.

sections.h2: What if the house is inherited, rented or facing foreclosure?
sections.html:
Each situation runs on a clock. Estates with up to $150,000 non-exempt can use summary administration, creditors file within three months of publication or 30 days of service, whichever is later, and foreclosure sales follow judgment by 20 to 35 days.

Tenants receive a 3 day nonpayment notice and 7 days to cure many breaches. These facts affect offers, so assemble the documents first.

sections.h2: How does Pembroke Pines handle public safety and services that buyers ask about?
sections.html:
The city's fire rescue department runs six stations, and Pembroke Pines became the South Region answering point in the Broward County Regional 911 system in 2014. The department earned a Class 1 ISO rating in 1998, which the city's history says only 57 of 44,000 departments held then.

Insurance rating and response data are useful to mention to buyers, and your agent can confirm the current rating for your address.

sections.h2: What about tax certificates and tax deeds in Pembroke Pines?
sections.html:
Unpaid taxes turn delinquent April 1, with certificates sold by June 1. After two years a holder can apply for a tax deed with a $75 application fee, and the clerk runs the auction.

The opening bid on a homestead includes one half of the latest assessed value. If you are behind, ask the Broward tax collector for a payoff and weigh a sale before a deed application.

  • Installment prepayment requires an application by May 1.
  • Senior deferral uses Form DR-570 by March 31.

sections.h2: Can seniors and veterans cut a Pembroke Pines tax bill?
sections.html:
Owners 65 or older may get an additional exemption of up to $50,000 if the local ordinance allows and income is within limit. Disabled veterans may receive a $5,000 assessed value reduction, and veterans 65 or older with a service-connected disability may get a discount equal to the VA percentage.

Deployed servicemembers may receive an exemption proportional to the time deployed, and may rent out a homestead without abandoning it. Ask the property appraiser about proof needed.

sections.h2: What are the risks of an informal family transfer in Pembroke Pines?
sections.html:
Moving legal or beneficial title counts as a change of ownership for assessment, with exceptions for spouses and some transfers at death, and quit claim deeds carry stamp tax.

The statute wants a written conveyance signed before two witnesses, so have a title agent prepare it.

sections.h2: What steps lead from offer to closing in Pembroke Pines?
sections.html:
Once you accept, a title agent searches title, gathers payoffs and drafts the deed, which needs two witnesses. The clerk then records it and collects the tax.

  • Put the doc stamp payer in the contract.
  • Order mortgage payoff and association statements.
  • Check your exemption status before the tax split.
  • Have permit and inspection records ready for the buyer inspector.

Pembroke Pines is one of the largest of more than 400 Florida municipalities, so recent sales near you should be plentiful and easy to compare.

sections.h2: Which services and amenities do Pembroke Pines buyers ask about?
sections.html:
The city says it counts 41 arts and cultural facilities, plus parks, golf courses and tree lined neighborhoods. It cites recognition as an All-America City and describes its mission as fostering a place to live, work and raise a family.

Its fire rescue department began as a volunteer group in 1953, hired its first three full-time employees in 1973 and today serves from six stations. The city history also records Station 69 opening in 1978 and Station 101 with a communications center in 2001. Buyers care about response times and insurance ratings, so ask your insurer what rating applies to your address, and keep the answer with your sale documents for buyers who ask later.

sections.h2: What steps should I take to prepare a Pembroke Pines sale?
sections.html:
Start with paperwork. Collect your deed, the latest tax bill, any association documents, and permit records for roofs, windows or additions.

Then weigh a listing, a private sale and a cash offer by your net proceeds. Insist on a written offer and read every line.

faqs.q: What year did Pembroke Pines incorporate?
faqs.a: 1960, on January 16 by the city's account, when it was a village of about 1,500 people.

faqs.q: Which doc stamp rate does Pembroke Pines use?
faqs.a: Seventy cents per $100 of consideration paid, because Broward is not Miami-Dade, as the state revenue page lists.

faqs.q: Can I keep my Save Our Homes savings?
faqs.a: Possibly. Portability may carry as much as $500,000 of the difference to a new Florida homestead.
Under the state rule each party stays liable, so write the payer into the contract.

faqs.q: Is an inherited Pembroke Pines house taxed when it transfers?
faqs.a: Deeds from a personal representative under a probated will are listed as untaxed, while other transfers can be taxed, so check with a title agent.
